certification: T6 model fitted by pooled within-day OLS on the minutes of the valid window days (at least 2 of 3); S60_cert = summed |impulse response| over 60 minutes, GM_cert = S60_cert/|h0|, U_cert = 95th percentile of |normalized flow| over the window; fixed for the whole evaluation day
data: Binance USD-M futures, the 20 thin symbols of Parts 6 and 9; evaluation days = the 28th of each month (train 2024, test 2025-01 to 2026-09); certification window = the 25th-27th of the same month; none of these days was used in Parts 1-11; validation V1-V5 unchanged
inference: 2,000 date-block bootstrap draws; secondary Holm-adjusted (bootstrap share of draws >= 0 as one-sided p)
primary: log TLR(amp_cert) - log TLR(vol) < 0 with the 95% date-block bootstrap interval below 0
question: Does a guard whose operator is certified from the previous three days lower tail loss per unit of position in thin books, compared with a volatility limit? (Part 6 estimated the operator from six hours and failed.)

rules.amp_cert (primary): R = rv_360 * GM_cert^theta, theta in {0, .25, .5, .75, 1} chosen on training TLR
rules.guard_6h: R = U6 * S60 (six-hour estimate, as Part 6)

runs: Q6 is run once; every run is counted in prereg/test_set_unlocks_p12.json
score: TLR = ES95(loss) / mean(q) on the test hours
secondary: guard_cert vs guard_6h (does certification improve the guard?)
sizing: q = c_s / R with c_s setting the training mean of q to 1 per symbol and rule; risk winsorized at training 1%/99%
unit: symbol-hour, hours 6-23 UTC of the evaluation day; loss = position x next-hour MAE
